$comment: D-CSUBSET-PER-MEMBER-PACKED: GNU `packed` on ONE struct member-declarator packs THAT member alone. struct P { char c; unsigned v <packed>; double d; } is sizeof 16 / _Alignof 8 with c@0 v@1 d@8 — the SAME size and the SAME alignment as the undecorated struct, which places v@4. Only the offset moves, which is why this example asserts offsets: exit = sizeof(16) + offsetof(v)(1) + offsetof(d)(8) + 17 = 42, and an unpacked member gives 16+4+8+17 = 45. A MISALIGNED 4-byte member at offset 1 is read+written at RUNTIME — the empirical proof codegen needs no per-member-packed fork (arm64 LDUR/STUR, x86 mov). Data-model-independent, so the one exit code holds on all four targets incl. the shipped release pipeline. REFERENCE-ORACLED: gcc 13.3.0 (x86_64 + aarch64), clang 18.1.3 (x86_64 + aarch64) and mingw-w64 gcc 13.2.0 each COMPILE AND RUN this file to 42; MSVC 19.51 abstains (no __attribute__ in any position).
